headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared workspace/MCP plus auto-execute-capable coding agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Semantic Kernel can use MCP servers and application-defined files, while Windsurf reads workspace files, uses clipboard, and also uses MCP. That creates a plausible default bridge where attacker-controlled content from one agent can be treated as instructions by the other. The pathway is not proven high because no raw web-content parser is documented here.
conditions: IF either agent ingests the other’s file or MCP output as instructions without provenance checks
IF shared workspace content is copied into Windsurf clipboard-driven workflows
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Route inter-agent messages through a provenance-tagged JSON schema
Add a manual review step before any MCP output is executed
Restrict both agents to separate workspaces
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization on all shared channels

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches application context and has broad network egress; agent B touches source code/open files and can read/write workspace files. If they share a workspace or memory store, sensitive code or context can flow from B into A’s model calls or external APIs. The evidence does not show PHI or secrets by default, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or memory store
IF either agent forwards file contents to an external model provider
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Turn off sharing of raw file contents to model calls where possible
Review outbound API destinations for both agents
Limit B’s workspace to non-sensitive repos
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad filesystem write and read access, and Windsurf additionally modifies git state while Semantic Kernel can write application-defined files. In a shared directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The pair’s concurrency models explicitly allow multiple instances, so the conflict pathway exists in default use.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or repository
IF Windsurf auto-commits or edits git state while Semantic Kernel writes files concurrently
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree
Pause one agent before the other writes
Disable auto-commit or auto-execute features
Use file locks around shared outputs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel can produce tool outputs and application context that Windsurf may consume while acting on code. Windsurf has terminal execution subject to Cascade auto-execute, so if it treats A’s output as authoritative, a mistaken or injected instruction can cascade into irreversible file or command actions. This is a default-dangerous interaction because one agent can operationalize the other’s output.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses Semantic Kernel output as authoritative input
IF Cascade auto-execute is enabled or command approval is bypassed
mitigations: Require human verification before any command derived from A’s output
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
Constrain A to emit structured, non-executable outputs
Log and diff all proposed actions before execution
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in the profiles, so only a limited compliance concern is supported. The main issue is that Windsurf is closed-source and handles source code/open files while Semantic Kernel can send context to external model providers, but the profiles do not establish a concrete regulatory breach. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined data flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared workspace
IF outbound model calls process data subject to a stricter residency or retention rule
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Review vendor terms for retention and residency
Use separate tenants for regulated projects
Document data-class handling for both tools
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls
